question.prompt: From time \(t=0\) to time \(t=1\) a population increased by \(i\%,\) and from time \(t=1\) to time \(t=2\) the population increased by \(j\%.\) Therefore, from time \(t=0\) to time \(t=2\) the population increased by

solutions.explanation:
The second increase is calculated from the population after the first increase. Let \(P>0\) be the initial population. An increase of \(i\%\) multiplies it by \(1+i/100\), so the population at time \(2\) is
\[
P_2=P\left(1+\frac{i}{100}\right)
       \left(1+\frac{j}{100}\right).
\]
Expanding and subtracting the original population gives the fractional increase
\[
\frac{P_2-P}{P}
=\frac{i+j}{100}+\frac{ij}{10000}.
\]
Multiplying this fraction by \(100\) expresses it as a percentage. The total increase is therefore \(\boxed{\left(i+j+\frac{ij}{100}\right)\%}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Multiply the growth factors
